First review of this head. The net diff against main is the four files above; the `packages/cli` paths a diff against the older merge base shows are main's own #33879, merged in, and are not this PR's.

### ① Derived judgments

The rule the gate must keep: an authenticated subject is handed an authorization code for a client only after the host's `oidcAuthorizeGate` admitted that subject to that client.

- **Every client the endpoint can act on is judged.** Read against the pinned provider: on any one pass the authorize endpoint takes its client from exactly one parameter source, and the gate now reads both sources the transport hands the hook, so the set it judges is a superset of the one client the provider can act on. The provider accepts a client only as a single non-empty string; the gate judges that same string, unchanged.
- **Request object and pushed request.** The pinned provider refuses a request object outright. A pushed request is refused unless a resolver is configured, and `plugin-auth` configures none; were one configured, the provider keeps the client the request itself named, which is the judged one. Neither form can introduce an unjudged client.
- **Resume passes.** Sign-in resume, `/oauth2/consent`, `/oauth2/continue` and the callback resumes all re-enter the authorize endpoint through the provider's hook-running dispatch, so the same gate runs on each, on the signature-checked request. The diff does not change that; the new describe pins three of them with a denying leg and an admitting control.
- **Fail closed.** A source that is not a plain object names nothing, and the provider then has no client to issue for. A present value that is not a string is judged by its string form, never skipped; the provider refuses such a value itself. A gate that throws ends the request. A request naming no client is not judged and cannot be issued a code. The unauthenticated fall-through is the declared ADR-0069 D5.1 contract and is unchanged.
- **Legitimate single-client flows.** A request naming one client once, or the same client in both sources, is judged once (the de-duplication, pinned). The one flow that newly moves is a request naming two different clients, which the changeset declares. I found no resume endpoint whose validated body carries a second client name into the gate.
- **Refusal delivery.** `oauth-authorize-refusal.ts` is unchanged and follows a redirect only on the strict form its header states; the newly judged form is answered with the envelope or the page, as the new pin asserts.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch` is the level AGENTS.md prescribes: `Metadata-protocol: none`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The carriers are all present and agree between PR body and changeset: `fix(auth)!:` title, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, a `**BREAKING**` paragraph, exactly one disposition marker, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with a reason that fits (nothing stored, no key or value retired, callback signature unchanged). That marker forbids a FROM/TO block and the body carries none; who moves, what changes for them and what stays are stated in prose.

CI on this head: 57 check-runs, 37 success, 20 skipped, none running, none failed; `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core` (8/8 shards) and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green. The three dogfood shards are skipped on a pull request by design and run on the merge queue, so the new dogfood legs are unmeasured by CI on this head; the body's dogfood reading is from an earlier commit of the branch and says a re-run on the final head is owed. I do not hold the verdict for it: the queue runs those shards before landing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No published schema, no governed path and no skill or hand-written docs page is in the diff; `Skills-docs: none` holds for what I could search.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` is outside the diff and carries the host-facing statement of the callback (S2).
- Open PR 33268 edits the same insertion point; a mechanical conflict for whichever lands second, as the body says.
- Adjacent surfaces that hand a subject tokens without passing `/oauth2/authorize` are outside this PR's stated scope and were not reviewed.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real: ADR-0069 D5.1 already says no code without the gate's admission, and the tree now keeps that for every client the endpoint can act on. It takes nothing away from a host or a client that the published contract granted. Judging both sources on every pass, rather than mirroring the provider's choice of source, is the right shape: it cannot drift when the provider's reading changes.

S1 (should-fix) — the pins cover less than the body and changeset say. The leg titled for a body naming two clients holds for the ordering it sends and not for the other, so it does not pin "refused if any one is refused" for that source; and no leg reaches the repeated-parameter arm or the non-string arm of `authorizeRequestClientIds`, so removing either arm leaves every test green. The tree keeps the rule in each of those cases today (the provider refuses them itself); the gap is that the fail-closed edge the PR declares is unpinned. Add a leg per arm, and retitle or re-shape the two-client leg so its name is what it measures. Detail is in the seat's notes, not here.

S2 (should-fix) — the `oidcAuthorizeGate` jsdoc in `auth-manager.ts` is where a host reads the callback's contract, and it still speaks of one requesting client per call site; the changeset's "can now be called once for each distinct client the request names" belongs there too, since the changeset text leaves the tree at release.

N1 (nit) — the changeset's "each a string or an array" describes the collector's input, not what a caller can send through every transport; one clause saying so would keep a host from reading it as a promise.

No must-fix.

This PASS is therefore a verdict on the tree as read, with no machine measurement of the five new legs behind it beyond the author's own stated readings. Plainly, for the seat: do not act on this record as a landing record. The conflict must be resolved first, that makes a new head, and the new head owes its own delta record and a green run that includes `Test Core`; the dogfood shards stay unmeasured until the merge queue, as before.

With the arm removed the request is still refused, so the envelope assertion alone would not catch it; the leg's assertion that the gate was asked about the refused client by itself is what goes red, in both orders. With the arm changed to skip such a value the gate is never asked and the same assertion goes red.
- `a resume pass whose body names a client_id that is not a string is judged on that value, and refused when it is refused` pins the non-string arm. With such values skipped, only the admitted client is judged and a code is handed out: red on both assertions. With the string coercion dropped, the recorded call no longer equals the expected string form: red. The refusal it reads is the gate's own, not the provider's, because the provider would have issued on this pass.
- `a form body naming client_id twice is handed no code unless the gate judged and admitted the client` (both orders) is the re-shaped two-client leg. Its title is now what it measures and it holds in either order; it goes red when the body source is not collected. It pins the body source, not an ordering, which is the honest reading of that transport.

N3 (nit): the PR body's quick-verify line still expects 27 tests where its own Readings say 31 on this head, and it lists the non-string leg under the resume describe while the tree has it in the first describe.
